Work can feel more manageable when people have a common place to see what is coming. A shared project calendar can provide that place, giving colleagues a way to view upcoming work together. But creating a shared view is only part of the story. The way people use that view, and the information they need from it, matters just as much.

That is where listening comes in. Gathering feedback from colleagues can reveal needs that may not be obvious from the calendar alone. A conversation about what people find useful can help connect the practical work of coordination with the people who rely on it.

In this article, we will explore the relationship between coordination and listening through the example of a shared project calendar. We will consider why a common view of upcoming work matters and how feedback can help bring colleagues' needs into the discussion. Whether you are thinking about a calendar or reflecting on the way your team shares information, the goal is to make room for a more thoughtful conversation about working together.
